 -2-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:7383  MFA No. 201343 of 2021 HC-KAR  THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the Judgment and award dated 24.07.2020 passed in MVC No.148/2015 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Sindagi (for short 'the tribunal'),
seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. The claimant was doing agriculture and also working as coolie.
The claimant met with accident on 09.12.2014 and sustained grievous injuries.
The claimant filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.23,90,000/-.
After considering the entire evidence on record, the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,09,880/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Aggrieved by the said order, the claimant preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation and mainly contended that, the claimant was earning a sum of Rs.9,000/- per NC: 2025:KHC-K:7383 HC-KAR month, but the tribunal has taken only Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Doctor has assessed the disability at 25%, but the tribunal has taken only 8%.
Further, it is stated that, the amounts granted under different heads are also meager and requested for enhancement of the compensation.
3. Heard the arguments from both sides.
4. The claimant has not filed any income proof.
He met with accident on 09.12.2014.
As per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the income of the claimant for the year 2014 is Rs.7,500/- per month.
The claimant was aged 46 years as on the date of the accident.

Hence,
the multiplier is '13'.

As per the Ex.P.10 and the evidence of Doctor, the claimant sustained (i)
Hemorrhage confirm seen in both frontal lobes, (ii) Minimal SAH seen in both tentoriumous falx,
(iii) fracture of right thig parietal bone (iv) Tenderness present over scalp more on R side.
There is no fracture to the skull as per X-ray.
Tenderness is present over scalp on right side, therefore, the Doctor assessed 25% as neurological disability.
Hence, the tribunal NC: 2025:KHC-K:7383 HC-KAR has rightly considered 1/3rd of 25% i.e. 8%.
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the disability assessed by the tribunal.

Hence, the loss of future earning capacity is as under:
Rs.7,500/- X 12 X 13 X 8% = Rs.93,600/-.

2 5.

The claimant was hospitalized for a period of 20 days and incurred Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses and the tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.

Considering the nature of the injuries, occupation and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering,
Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The claimant might have not attended any other work for at least four months.
Hence, a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rs.7,500/- X 4 months) is awarded towards loss of income during laid up period.

Hence, the total compensation is as follows:

Learned counsel for the Insurance company submits that, the compensation amount awarded by the tribunal has been deposited before the tribunal.
